problem: Let $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where ${b}_{1}=2{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=-5{c}_{1}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Writing a Two-Dimensional Vector in a Different Basis
examples.problem: Let $\mathcal{B}= \left\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \right\}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065354/assets/acda5be1511b340b3a947cbaa4dedfd7a3175029d2937481b261c7a0c4eb5348.png) What are the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}= \left\{ \mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{c}_2 \right\},$ where $\mathbf{c}_1 = -\mathbf{b}_2$ and $\mathbf{c}_2 = -3\mathbf{b}_1?$
examples.worked_solution:
Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065354/assets/ac75a1bca2b8012016657f4d1d88fdf1725c84b2a3ec48376bbcb4670f134ba3.png) we can write $\mathbf{x}$ in terms of the vectors $\mathbf c_1$ and $\mathbf c_2,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\  & =-2{b}_{2}+5{b}_{1} \\  & =2(-{b}_{2})-\frac{5}{3}(-3{b}_{1}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}-\frac{5}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065354/assets/d98192a7e16e605311ee2bb8791e6d86005c6d565ede80e68aaaeaf8097721a2.png)
